Elevations experience greater downward pressure than valleys, causing material to flow laterally until equilibrium is reached. This process leads to a uniform radial distribution, resulting in spherical geometry. The mathematical framework relies on hydrostatic equilibrium equations where net force vanishes at each point. Dualities emerge between empirical observation (e.g., celestial bodies) and theoretical deduction (e.g., Newtonian gravity). Failure modes occur when external forces (rotation, tidal effects) or insufficient mass prevent equilibrium. The logical hierarchy ensures that conclusions derived from theory align with empirical data, validating the model's robustness.
